edition.locus: De Trinitate XI (Verbum caro / utraque substantia)

source_text: Quis igitur dubitet, cum in extrema parte dicitur: Verbum caro factum est, et habitauit in nobis, Christum, cuius est natiuitas, et quia caro factus est, esse hominem, et quia uerbum Dei, Deum incunctanter edicere esse, praesertim cum animaduertat scripturam euangelicam utramque istam substantiam in unam natiuitatis Christi foederasse concordiam? 4. Hic est enim qui sicut sponsus egreditur de thalamo suo, exultauit ut gigas ad currendam uiam; a summo caelo egressio eius et usque ad summum regressio eius, quoniam usque ad summum nec quisquam in caelum ascendit, nisi qui de caelo descendit; Filius hominis qui est in caelis.
pass_a_gloss: Who therefore would-doubt, when in extreme part it-is-said: Word flesh has-been-made, and dwelt in us, Christ, whose is nativity, and because flesh he-has-been-made, to-be human, and because word of-God, God without-hesitation to-declare to-be, especially when he-notices scripture evangelical both that substance into one of-nativity of-Christ to-have-covenanted concord? This is for who as bridegroom goes-out from chamber his, he-exulted as giant toward to-run way; from highest heaven going-out of-him and unto unto-highest return of-him, because unto unto-highest neither anyone into heaven has-ascended, except who from heaven has-descended; Son of-human who is in heavens.

lemmas.form: in unam natiuitatis Christi foederasse concordiam
lemmas.gloss: bound into one concord of Christ’s nativity

pass_b_english: Who then would doubt — when at the end it is said, “The Word became flesh and dwelt among us” — that Christ, whose birth it is, is human because he became flesh, and is God because he is the Word of God, and would not hesitate to say so, especially when he notices that the evangelical Scripture has bound both those substances into one concord of Christ’s nativity?

For this is the one who “goes out from his chamber like a bridegroom; he exulted like a giant to run the course; his going out is from the highest heaven and his return is to the highest,” since no one has gone up to the highest into heaven except the one who came down from heaven — the Son of Man who is in the heavens.

choices.term: utramque istam substantiam in unam natiuitatis Christi foederasse concordiam
choices.english: bound both those substances into one concord of Christ’s nativity
choices.why: Two substances (God/human) united in one birth — not two Christs.
rejected: merged both substances into a birth mash-up

choices.english: to declare without hesitation that he is God
choices.why: Word → God as plainly as flesh → human.
rejected: to soft-announce he might be God-ish
